Package org.checkerframework.framework.util.defaults

Class QualifierDefaults

java.lang.Object
org.checkerframework.framework.util.defaults.QualifierDefaults
public class QualifierDefaults extends Object
Determines the default qualifiers on a type. Default qualifiers are specified via the DefaultQualifier annotation.

Type variable uses have two possible defaults. If flow sensitive type refinement is enabled, unannotated top-level type variable uses receive the same default as local variables. All other type variable uses are defaulted using the TYPE_VARIABLE_USE default. 


 <T> void method(USE T tIn) {
     LOCAL T t = tIn;
 }
The parameter tIn will be defaulted using the TYPE_VARIABLE_USE default. The local variable t will be defaulted using the LOCAL_VARIABLE default, in order to allow dataflow to refine T.

    • permittedAtLocation

      public boolean permittedAtLocation(AnnotationMirror anno, TypeUseLocation location)
      Does anno's TargetLocations meta-annotation permit it at location?

      A qualifier can restrict where it may be written via TargetLocations. Defaulting a qualifier onto a prohibited location causes type validation errors on code the user did not write.

      Parameters:
      anno - a qualifier
      location - a type use location
      Returns:
      true if anno may be applied at location

    • permittedAtProgrammaticLocation

      public boolean permittedAtProgrammaticLocation(AnnotationMirror anno, TypeUseLocation location)
      Returns true if anno may be applied at location as a programmatic default (e.g., via addCheckedCodeDefault(javax.lang.model.element.AnnotationMirror, org.checkerframework.framework.qual.TypeUseLocation, boolean), addUncheckedCodeDefault(org.checkerframework.framework.util.defaults.QualifierDefaults.UncheckedDefaultsMode, javax.lang.model.element.AnnotationMirror, org.checkerframework.framework.qual.TypeUseLocation, boolean), or addElementDefault(javax.lang.model.element.Element, javax.lang.model.element.AnnotationMirror, org.checkerframework.framework.qual.TypeUseLocation)).

      If anno carries a ProgrammaticDefaultLocations meta-annotation, its locations are checked. Otherwise, falls back to permittedAtLocation(AnnotationMirror, TypeUseLocation).

      A qualifier may explicitly specify its allowed programmatic default locations via ProgrammaticDefaultLocations. If omitted, top and bottom qualifiers in the qualifier hierarchy are permitted at all locations for programmatic defaults (as the canonical bounds of the lattice), while other qualifiers fall back to permittedAtLocation(javax.lang.model.element.AnnotationMirror, org.checkerframework.framework.qual.TypeUseLocation).

      Parameters:
      anno - the annotation mirror to check
      location - the location
      Returns:
      true if anno may be used as a programmatic default at location

    • addElementDefault

      public void addElementDefault(Element elem, AnnotationMirror elementDefaultAnno, TypeUseLocation location)
      Sets the default annotations for a certain Element.

      This default is combined with any written @DefaultQualifier annotations on the element and inherits the defaults of enclosing elements, no matter in which order the defaults of elem, of its enclosing elements, or of its members were queried while the type factory was being initialized.

      This is an initialization-time API: it must be called while the type factory is being created, such as from GenericAnnotatedTypeFactory.createQualifierDefaults() or GenericAnnotatedTypeFactory.addCheckedCodeDefaults(org.checkerframework.framework.util.defaults.QualifierDefaults). Calling it after type checking has begun throws a TypeSystemError, because types that have already been computed and dataflow results that have already been produced are never recomputed, and diagnostics that have already been issued cannot be retracted, so the new default would apply to some of the program and not to the rest of it.

      If the registered default conflicts with a @DefaultQualifier written on elem -- same location and same qualifier hierarchy, but a different qualifier -- then a TypeSystemError is thrown later, when elem's defaults are computed. Only one qualifier from a hierarchy can be the default for a location, so a type system must not register one that contradicts what a user is permitted to write.

      Parameters:
      elem - the scope to set the default within
      elementDefaultAnno - the default to set
      location - the location to apply the default to
      Throws:
      TypeSystemError - if called after type checking has begun

    • checkConflictingDefaults

      public void checkConflictingDefaults(Element elt, Tree tree)
      Reports each pair of elt's own written @DefaultQualifier annotations that set the same TypeUseLocation in the same qualifier hierarchy to different qualifiers.

      Called by the visitor for a declaration in source, so that the diagnostic does not depend on whether anything happened to ask for elt's defaults: defaultsAtDirect(javax.lang.model.element.Element) runs on a cache miss, and for a package whose package-info.java is the only file compiled it never runs at all. The winner is decided by source order, as it is there.

      Parameters:
      elt - a declaration in source
      tree - the declaration of elt, on which the errors are reported

    • applyPermissiveDefaults

      public boolean applyPermissiveDefaults(Element annotationScope)
      Given an element, returns whether the permissive default should be applied for it. Handles elements from bytecode or source code.

      At most one of this and applyConservativeDefaults(javax.lang.model.element.Element) returns true for an element: a kind of code cannot be defaulted both permissively and conservatively, which SourceChecker rejects at startup.

      Parameters:
      annotationScope - the element that the permissive default might apply to
      Returns:
      whether the permissive default applies to the given element
